turns.prompt:
Create a tailings dam risk map and control board for a tailings dam risk review. This is a presentation artifact, not an interactive dashboard. Keep it as one tailings dam risk map and control board in the first viewport.

Situation: Site: Copper Ridge. Cells C1-C3, seepage point SP2, piezometer PZ-8, downstream creek, storm forecast, pump station PS1, community liaison.
Current state: PZ-8 pressure 12% above trigger red, SP2 seepage amber, C2 freeboard 0.7 m, storm forecast 45 mm, PS1 pump 68% capacity, creek monitor normal.
Timeline: 06:00 geotech read, 07:15 seepage walkdown, 08:20 storm forecast, 09:00 pump test, 11:00 regulator call, 15:00 community update.
Sources: S1 geotech dashboard, S2 seepage log, S3 weather forecast, S4 pump telemetry, S5 creek monitor, S6 regulator note.

Requirements: 1. The first viewport must be dominated by one coherent visual artifact, not a grid of detached KPI cards. 2. Show the main entities, current states, source markers S1-S6, timeline, legend, and four connected callouts. 3. The callouts must cover PZ-8 trigger, SP2 seepage, C2 freeboard, storm forecast. 4. Use polished domain-appropriate styling with readable labels and no critical overlap.

Reframe it for the environmental regulator. Preserve the risk map; add exactly three controls: lower pond level, staff SP2 watch, pre-stage pump PS1. Add two leader-linked lenses for piezometer trend and storm rainfall.

Update at 12:30: PZ-8 falls to 6% above trigger amber, SP2 seepage clears, storm forecast rises to 62 mm red, PS1 pump increases to 84% capacity. Synchronize map, controls, timeline, source tags, callouts, and change note. Do not leave SP2 as active seepage.
Create a regulator incident page. Fit risk map, control ledger, source tags S1-S6, confidence markers, freeboard/storm strip, and timeline in the first viewport.
Add a community update card beside the incident page. It must preserve PZ-8 amber, SP2 clear, storm 62 mm red, PS1 84%, creek normal, and source markers.
